current_focus.domain: navigator detail: what a row tap does on the wide (600dp+) layout, where the in-app detail pane can never be filled because selection hands off to the GitHub app
current_focus.summary: navigator-detail-017: wide (600dp+) row tap fills the in-app detail pane beside the list; second tap on the highlighted row or the pane's Open on GitHub opens the GitHub app in split view. Narrow (cover display) row tap raises a modal detail sheet over the full-width list with Open on GitHub; replaces 'detail replaces the list'. Long-press opens GitHub on both widths, unchanged. Bounded to NavigatorScreen plus stable test tags on detail pane, sheet and Open on GitHub; debug picker stays dev-only. Preserve navigator-scope-005 chrome, truth rules, read-only, CI floor; update features/navigator.md and re-drive it with the helpers; cover-display steps maintainer-gated; proof under proof/navigator-detail-20260918/PROOF.md with capture SHA-256s. Excluded: posture emulation, GitHub writes, commit/PR until asked. Maintainer confirmed 2026-09-18 after trying the hybrid preview on the live picker.

decisions.choice: Compact widget uses a right-aligned ledger composition: repository name on top, then label-left/number-right rows — 'issues N', 'PRs N', and 'to review N'. Type shrinks so rows fit at the declared 120x64dp COMPACT_SIZE floor; the 'to review' row is progressive disclosure that appears when height allows. Counts come from live data: one GET /repos/{owner}/{name} per refresh supplies open_issues_count, and true issues = open_issues_count - openPrs (GitHub counts PRs as issues). Basis falls back to LAST_GOOD when the open-PR list is itself page-truncated, never rendering a bound as an exact count. Selected in picker round compact-widget-content-round-2 (round 1 rejected: five wordings of one layout read as the same widget). Scope: compact slot only; the tall row feed stays on fixtures for a later cycle.

decisions.question: Who can install the GitHub App once the product is public?
decisions.rationale: A public product cannot hardcode the maintainer's installation topology; supersedes github-app-topology-006 while preserving its sign-in and no-cookie rules.

decisions.choice: Maintainer delivery rides the proven SwarmPocket rail, generalized: merge an app change -> CI builds and publishes the APK to a rolling GitHub release -> cp-1 pulls it within 30 minutes -> the update banner appears on the phone over WireGuard -> one-tap install. The public rolling release doubles as the public sideload channel; the cp-1 puller and banner configuration stay swarm-side so the product keeps zero swarm dependency. First device install is one manual sideload (REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES for self-update); release signing keystore and CI secrets are maintainer-gated.

history.note: Play Store pivot (maintainer 2026-08-16): RepoGlance ships via the Play Store and versions via semver Git tags, so the SwarmPocket-style rolling-release / cp-1-puller / one-tap-banner rail is retired. Replaced by release-model-013 (tag-driven GitHub Releases + Play Store); implemented in PR #8; swarmpocket #29 and RepoGlance canary #3 closed as superseded.

decisions.question: How do merged app changes reach the maintainer's phone (and the public)?
decisions.rationale: Maintainer's stated pipeline: 'merge an app change -> CI builds and publishes to a rolling release -> cp-1 pulls it within 30 minutes -> the pink banner appears on your phone -> one tap'. Implementable only once the build lane produces an APK and CI exists.

decisions.choice: Version RepoGlance with semver Git tags (OpenClaw-style vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH plus -beta.N). Pushing a tag runs release.yml, which builds a signed AAB + APK and publishes a GitHub Release (APK + SHA256SUMS attached, curated changelog body); versionCode is derived monotonically from the tag. The per-push rolling canary is dropped -- releases are cut only on tags. The Play Store becomes the primary distribution and update channel for the maintainer's phone and the public, with the AAB uploaded to a Play internal track via a service account. Release signing (upload keystore) and CI/Play secrets are maintainer-gated.

decisions.rationale: Maintainer 2026-08-16: 'I plan to add repoglance to play store eventually so this is all pointless... let's just plan to version repoglance with GitHub tags similar to how OpenClaw keeps up with their versions.' Once the Play Store is the update channel, the in-house daemon-served self/companion update rail (swarmpocket #29, built on #28's self-update-over-tunnel) and the cp-1 rolling-release puller are vestigial. Implemented in PR #8; swarmpocket #29 and RepoGlance canary #3 closed as superseded.

decisions.baseline_ref: git:b445dc4 NavigatorScreen wide branch openGitHubOnSelect=true; DetailPane reads 'Select a row to see details'
decisions.choice: Wide (600dp+): candidate C from round navigator-detail-round-1 — a row tap fills the in-app detail pane beside the list; a second tap on the highlighted row (or the pane's Open on GitHub) opens the item in the GitHub app in split view. Narrow (cover display): maintainer-requested hybrid — a row tap raises a modal detail sheet over the full-width list (D's sheet) instead of replacing the list; Open on GitHub in the sheet. Long-press on a row opens GitHub on both widths, unchanged. The narrow behaviour recorded by feature-map-015 (nav-row-narrow: detail replaces the list) is superseded by this decision and features/navigator.md is updated accordingly.
decisions.domain: navigator detail: what a row tap does on the wide (600dp+) layout, where the in-app detail pane can never be filled because selection hands off to the GitHub app

history.choice: Undecided — five candidates (A pane-fill, B list-only, C second-tap, D sheet, E single-pane) in picker round navigator-detail-round-1; awaiting the maintainer's pick from device captures.

decisions.question: On the wide (600dp+) navigator layout, what does a row tap do, given that today it hands off to the GitHub app and the in-app detail pane can never be filled?
decisions.rationale: Maintainer on the live picker (2026-09-18): keep long-hold for GitHub; an opened Fold should default to split view; B or C for wide, C gives more; likes D's slide-up sheet but wants it on the closed phone, where today the list is replaced. Hybrid previewed for confirmation as a replacement for the five, not a sixth option; scope widened to the narrow slot by explicit maintainer choice ("both in this cycle").
